set_fields.description_long: The House passed H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, on May 22, 2025, by a vote of 215 to 214. The House Clerk’s roll call records the vote. In its June 4 estimate of the House-passed text, the Congressional Budget Office projected that federal Medicaid spending would be $840.2 billion lower and SNAP spending $267 billion lower over 2025–2034. CBO also estimated that 10.9 million more people would be uninsured in 2034 compared with its January 2025 baseline. These estimates apply to the version that passed the House and to the stated budget period; they are not observed outcomes or estimates of the later enacted law. The projection provides a baseline-based estimate of possible federal spending and coverage changes if that House text were implemented. The vote and projections describe two distinct facts: what the House passed and what CBO estimated about that version’s future effects.
